why: The output avoids must_not 1 but breaks must_not 2. On item 1: verifier Check 3 builds its list from every export and fails when any function is listed under `missing:`. It also says "Watch for slugify", so a README with only a padLeft section would fail. On item 2: Checks 1 and 2 use only single-character fills and don't add a parameter-count check, so they're fine. Check 3 is stricter than its line. Its regex only accepts a heading that starts with the exact, case-sensitive function name, optionally after a backtick. A real slugify section headed "## Slugify" or "## The slugify helper" would fail, so a README layout is effectively required. Check 4 is also stricter than "npm test passes". It requires the output to show the literal `# fail 0`, which depends on the test reporter: node --test's spec reporter doesn't print that line even when every test passes.
